--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We have parent slot 3 with fitness 267.799? Actually parent at slot3. Need improve. We have probes behavior."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 3 starts with ten C rounds, then classifies opponents and mostly cooperates against always-C. The trace simulates controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and population slots. It changes the strategy to probe/exploit never-defecting opponents, use forgiving TFT with recent-defection checks, and defect against high-defection opponents.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these measurements when deciding what to retain or change to maximize cumulative tournament fitness."
STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional strategy that starts with cooperation, probes/exploits always-cooperative opponents, retaliates against defection, and forgives low-defection opponents. The trace simulates this parent against TFT variants, slot8, always-C, and always-D opponents, computing round-by-round scores. It revises the parent by adding a probe at round 6, exploitation of opponents with zero defections, defection thresholds based on opponent defection rate, and forgiveness/punishment rules to break DD cycles and avoid exploitation.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got against slot8? We don't have parent measurement for slot8, but likely lower. So v4 is excellent against slot8 too."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, probes with a defection after five cooperative rounds, exploits never-defecting opponents, retaliates against unprovoked defections, forgives when it recently defected, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates this revised strategy against always-C, always-D, TFT, and slot8. It changes the probe/forgiveness logic to avoid double defections and to recover against TFT and slot8.
